references.text: The background to Israel's sin at Baal-Peor, where the people began to commit sexual immorality with Moabite women and bow down to their gods.
The account of Cozbi, daughter of a Midianite chief, who was killed by Phinehas along with the Israelite Zimri.
The names of those who were killed: Zimri and Cozbi, daughter of Zur, a tribal leader in Midian.
The Lord's command to take vengeance on the Midianites for their treachery against Israel.
Moses explains that it was Midianite women who led Israel into unfaithfulness toward the Lord at Peor, following Balaam's advice.
Moses reminds the people that the Lord destroyed all those who followed Baal-Peor.
Joshua mentions the sin at Peor as a warning to Israel.
The psalm describes Israel's sin at Baal-Peor and the plague that followed, as well as Phinehas' intervention.
Hosea notes that Israel devoted themselves to Baal-Peor and became as detestable as what they loved.
Revelation mentions Balaam's teaching that caused the Israelites to eat food sacrificed to idols and commit sexual immorality, a parallel to the event at Peor.
